name: create_trigger
description: Create a natural-language trigger owned by the current user. A trigger has three parts: an **if** condition (`trigger_nl_condition` — when to fire), a **fire message** (`trigger_fire_message` — what to deliver when it fires), and a **destination** (where to deliver). In v0 the only supported destination is `null`, which records the fire in the Event Log; outbound dispatch (webhook, agent message, etc.) isn't wired yet. Only call this after the user has explicitly asked to create a trigger — do not create speculatively.

scope_path.description: Wiki-relative path of the file or directory to watch. Use a `.md` path (e.g. `auth/passwords.md`) to watch one doc, or a directory path (e.g. `auth`) to watch every doc beneath it. Use an empty string for the wiki root.

trigger_nl_condition.description: **If condition.** Plain-language description of when the trigger should fire (e.g. "when the auth flow's session-timeout policy changes"). Evaluated by an LLM against the diff, so be specific about what kind of change matters.

trigger_fire_message.description: **What message to send.** The notification body delivered when the trigger fires (e.g. "Auth: session timeout policy changed — please review"). Will appear in the Event Log entry.

destination.description: **Where to send it.** Must be `null` in v0 — fires are recorded in the Event Log. Other destinations (webhook URLs, etc.) will be added later.
